answer: Agent economies stop sybils by making identity expensive. Each agent bonds stake and earns peer attestations, so a hollow crowd of clones has no trusted root to grow from. Real agents cultivate an orchard of mutual signatures; a sybil oasis of isolated bots stays barren and unverified, unable to sway outcomes. Because every fake persona must pay full stake yet earns no trust, mass impersonation becomes a net loss the attacker cannot profit from.
